title: Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing): Figuring the Refund on an Observation or Emergency Post-Payment Denial
content:
**What the denial reaches.** On an Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing), Riverbend treats a post-payment denial of an observation or emergency stay as reaching every service of the account except the diagnostic tests, which its payer agreements keep payable as outpatient diagnostics: the echocardiography (revenue code 0483), the electrocardiogram tracings (revenue code 0730), the laboratory tests (revenue code 0300), the computed tomography (revenue code 0350) and the contrast supply line (code Q9967 under revenue code 0636).

**The quantities**
- *Payment received*: the claim's payer payments less any payer recoveries already on the claim.
- *Diagnostic tests*: read from the charge postings of the Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) by their charges — the echocardiogram code 93306 under revenue code 0483, the tracing code 93005 under revenue code 0730, the laboratory codes 84484, 85025 and 80053 under revenue code 0300, the CT angiography code 71275 under revenue code 0350, the contrast code Q9967 under revenue code 0636, and every other charge under revenue codes 0483, 0730, 0300 and 0350.
- *Retained value*: the charges of the diagnostic tests multiplied by the payer class's expected allowed percentage of charges.
- *Retained payment*: the retained value.
- *Refund*: the payment received less the retained payment, never below 0.00.

**Assembly.** Each group of tests is valued first, never above the billed charges of the lines it values (Riverbend's agreements pay the lesser of the scheduled amount and the billed charges); a multiplier of their sum then applies to give the retained value, never above the charges of the diagnostic tests; any amount taken from the retained value comes after it (never below 0.00), giving the retained payment; the retained payment is then taken from the payment received (never below 0.00), and the total is rounded once. The refund is rounded to the nearest cent once, on the final total, and when it is 0.00 no entry is written.

**Worked example (hypothetical, payer class modeled at 50%).**
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Payer payments | 6,000.00 |
| Payer recoveries already on the claim | 500.00 |
| Payment received | 5,500.00 |
| Diagnostic test charges | 2,400.00 |
| Retained value and retained payment | 1,200.00 |
| Refund | 4,300.00 |
